title: Choose your tournament studio direction
question: The roll assigned Nocturnal Broadcast Studio (Candidate 5). Pick it, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Nocturnal Broadcast Studio
options.lineage: Modern FIDE / esports broadcast control room
options.thesis: A dark-slate tournament arena where the 64-square board anchors the room and authorized players quietly unlock an invisible side-rail operator console.
options.viewport: Top room bar with invite code and optional Sign In, centered tournament board with split-second clocks, and a clean move/chat rail (with hidden Ctrl+Shift+T troll drawer for authorized accounts).
options.risk: Falls flat into generic dark SaaS if board squares, clock hierarchy, and active-turn luminance lack contrast.

raised.raise: Strict mathematical type scale with zero arbitrary sizes between headings, notation, and clocks.
Clean separation between the immutable board coordinate ground and the crisp tactical/troll vector overlay.
Spatial registration keeps the central chessboard locked at one exact frame across lobby, match, and replay.
Compact single-click action grid inside the stealth operator drawer so troll powers trigger without scrolling.
Decisive sliding pill states for turn ownership, room readiness, and active troll toggles.

options.label: Broadcast Desk & Eval Ribbon
options.lineage: Live tournament broadcast desk (Freestyle / FIDE Grand Prix)
options.thesis: A sleek broadcast studio layout with horizontal match strip, warm-stone board squares, and electric cobalt turn focus.
options.viewport: Full-bleed top match bar above a wide board-plus-notation split, anchored by horizontal clock bands.
options.risk: Closely mirrors mainstream tournament broadcast conventions.

options.thesis: An ultra-crisp Swiss precision board studio where oversized tabular clocks and variable-weight notation lead the room.
options.viewport: Giant crisp countdown digits stack beside a stark square board, with one crimson accent marking active pressure and check.
options.case: Holds clarity strongly through disciplined tabular numerals and spatial calm; loses narrowly on classic dark tournament studio expectations.
options.risk: Can feel stark or clinical if piece silhouettes lack warmth.

options.thesis: Coarse pixel-grid chess labels and integer-stepped display banners over stark monochrome.
options.viewport: Blocky pixel clock digits flanking a stark monochrome board.
options.case: Loses both axes: pixel zine typography hurts rapid algebraic readability and breaks the requested sleek tournament studio feel.
options.kept: Strict mathematical type scale across sizes.

options.thesis: Terrain-coded forest board with purple tactical vector lines riding overhead.
options.viewport: Topographic terrain board with numbered purple move paths.
options.case: Loses both axes: forest/marsh map colors fight chess piece legibility and contradict the dark slate brief.
options.kept: Clean separation between fixed board ground and tactical vector overlay.
options.risk: Low contrast under fast blitz play.

options.thesis: Five warm-cream folio plates tracking match phases at fixed specimen scale.
options.viewport: Cream archival board framed by phase plates.
options.case: Loses both axes: warm archival cream folio conflicts with dark slate real-time multiplayer ergonomics.
options.kept: Fixed spatial registration across lobby, game, and replay states.

options.lineage: Event hall circle catalog on newsprint
options.thesis: Dense black-and-newsprint cell matrix packing every move and power into stamp squares.
options.viewport: Dense hall-map cell grid alongside a compact board.
options.case: Loses both axes: cramped newsprint density overwhelms players during real-time chess.
options.kept: Single-click compact cell grid inside the hidden troll drawer.

options.thesis: Playful apple-green and coral rounded lobes separating clocks, board, and room controls.
options.viewport: Curved coastline lobes holding a pastel board and bright capsule chips.
options.case: Loses both axes: playful park palette gives away the casual gag tone and distracts from a serious chess cover identity.
options.kept: Crisp capsule state-chip transitions for turn and toggle status.

canonCard.label: Modern Chess Platform Standard
canonCard.thesis: Familiar dark tournament chessboard flanked by opponent strip, clock box, and move list.
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar nav, central green-and-ivory board, right notation & chat panel.
canonCard.risk: Looks immediately recognizable as a clone of standard chess platforms.
